project.name: ReSono Labs R1 Voice
project.description: JackRabbit is a standalone, non-commercial community voice system for the Rabbit R1, combining a native HOME application, OpenAI Realtime voice, an on-device runtime with local storage, and browser-based management while preserving the working Rabbit/Cipher hardware foundation. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project and Product Spine
tour.description: Begin with JackRabbit’s public overview to understand the physical R1 product, current working capabilities, remaining delivery slices, repository structure, and non-commercial community boundary. This establishes that the native HOME, on-device runtime, browser management surface, and retained hardware substrate are one product rather than independent demos.

tour.title: Android Boot and Composition
tour.description: Move from product intent to the physical startup path: the boot receiver restores the runtime service, MainActivity becomes HOME, and ProductRootView composes real Voice, settings, navigation, and R1 input. The Android guide explains why presentation and hardware behavior stay native while provider and storage behavior remain outside the activity process.
tour.languageLesson: Android lifecycle callbacks and BroadcastReceiver entry points are framework-owned inversion-of-control hooks: the platform calls project code at boot, activity creation, focus changes, and teardown.

tour.title: Native Voice and Input
tour.description: With the HOME composition in view, follow the user’s physical interaction into VoicePageView and the hardware input router. NativeVoicePeer owns microphone, speaker, WebRTC, and the ordered Realtime data channel, while VoiceSessionStateTracker converts provider events into truthful idle, connecting, live, responding, and error states.
tour.languageLesson: The Java layer uses small interfaces and explicit state machines to isolate Android hardware events from feature rendering and provider-specific Realtime events.

tour.title: Runtime Trust Boundary
tour.description: Voice crosses into an isolated Android foreground service rather than running provider logic in the HOME activity. RuntimeService supervises embedded Python, RuntimePythonHost invokes its entrypoint, RuntimeSecretStore protects the loopback bearer token, and RuntimeCredentialBridge exposes only bounded Keystore-backed credential operations.
tour.languageLesson: Android process declarations and non-exported services form a security boundary; Java adapters then expose narrow capabilities to embedded Python without exporting raw Keystore keys.

tour.title: Python Runtime Lifecycle
tour.description: Inside that trusted host, entrypoint.py provides thread-safe start and stop operations and constructs RuntimeApplication as the composition root. RuntimeApplication wires storage, providers, agents, MCP, pairing, and HTTP serving, while ReleaseSupervisor provides atomic active and last-known-good release handling.
tour.languageLesson: Python composition roots keep object construction in one place, while a module-level lock and singleton runtime instance make the embedded start/stop contract explicit.

tour.title: Authenticated Local API
tour.description: The runtime exposes one authenticated loopback HTTP boundary for native clients and one paired HTTPS browser path through the Android host. HttpServer handles transport and SSE, RuntimeRoutes dispatches product operations, RuntimeEventStream carries live state, and PairingAuthority enforces one-time codes, origin binding, CSRF, token, and expiry checks.
tour.languageLesson: The Python HTTP boundary separates transport adapters from route dispatch, while server-sent events provide a simple one-way stream for truthful live runtime state.

tour.title: Providers Agents and MCP
tour.description: Building on the local API, ProviderController selects only runtime-reported providers, access paths, and models. The Platform and subscription adapters own their distinct credential and transport behavior, AgentsSdkTextRunner supplies the required text-agent path, and LocalMcpServer gives text and Voice one permission-filtered tool contract.
tour.languageLesson: Python Protocol-style boundaries and injected executors keep provider-specific HTTP and OAuth behavior behind one exercised product contract without creating a second agent loop.

tour.title: Sessions Memory and Retrieval
tour.description: Completed Voice sessions flow into canonical SQLite transcript and summary repositories before the memory pipeline invokes the single Agents SDK reviewer. Validated memory records receive real provider embeddings and are retrieved with bounded cosine ranking, preserving session provenance and deletion behavior throughout.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses model repository results, SQLite transactions preserve canonical state, and packed float vectors support cosine similarity without introducing a native vector database dependency.

tour.title: Browser Management Surface
tour.description: The browser uses the same runtime-backed state rather than a separate facade: index.html supplies semantic controls, app.js drives pairing, provider, session, and memory flows, and the shared CSS tokens preserve the Browser Voice visual language. The web guide makes the anti-mock and Android-packaging ownership rules explicit.
tour.languageLesson: Vanilla JavaScript event handlers coordinate authenticated fetch calls, while CSS custom properties provide a shared token vocabulary across responsive management states.

tour.title: Device Management Bridge
tour.description: The native settings surface and browser converge on real device management behavior through separate trusted adapters. SettingsPanelView presents actual hardware and OpenAI state, RuntimeManagementClient calls loopback APIs, ManagementHttpsServer serves paired LAN clients, and ManagementTlsIdentity maintains the Keystore-backed certificate for the currently advertised host.

tour.title: Build and Package Spine
tour.description: The clean Android build embeds the Python runtime, real management assets, WebRTC modules, and exact arm64 native dependencies into one APK. The debug build orchestrator stages assets and runs tests, the wheel script reproducibly cross-compiles hash-pinned native packages, and the package gate inspects the nested APK contents before an artifact can advance.
tour.languageLesson: Gradle Kotlin DSL defines module composition, while strict-mode Bash makes cross-toolchain packaging fail fast and hash checks bind native outputs to reviewed sources.

tour.title: Acceptance and Operations
tour.description: Finish with the evidence surfaces that keep architectural claims honest. The operational guide records verified build, ADB, runtime, database, and memory workflows; the boundary script rejects hosted or future-slice drift; and focused runtime tests exercise lifecycle, providers, sessions, memory, and failure behavior.
tour.languageLesson: Executable boundary checks complement unit tests: tests prove encoded behavior, while repository scans reject prohibited dependency and ownership patterns before packaging.
